highlights.title: Pennsylvania will require labels on AI-generated ads
highlights.summary: On Thursday, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro signed the Artificial Intelligence Deceptive Advertising Act into law, requiring disclosures on AI-generated ads. The law requires any ad - whether it's a still image, video, audio, or text - that "has been significantly modified or generated by…
body: Pennsylvania is one of the first states to require disclosures on AI content. And it requires those labels regardless of where an ad was created. So you might see disclosures pop up in commercials in other states if they’re also expected to air in Pennsylvania.

The law leaves many loopholes, though. For one, what constitutes “significantly modified” is subjective. There is also a carve-out for “parody, satire, commentary or criticism,” as well as anything that is “evidently fictional.” Again, what “evidently fictional” means is unclear. The wording also suggests only content that “uses synthetic content in a manner that creates a false consumer perception” about a product or service would require a disclosure. Again, leaving questions about what qualifies as “false” under the law and who makes those decisions.
The office of State Senator Nick Pisciottano, who introduced the bill, did not immediately return a request for comment.

Leclerc finished second fastest to McLaren's Lando Norris in Q1, but only after the McLaren driver completed a second run to do so, and then was then back at the head of the field in Q2.

highlights.title: 58 Years Later, Captain Kirk's Best Star Trek Quote Is the Greatest Line in Sci-Fi History
highlights.summary: Certain lines of dialogue become so famous they almost stop belonging to the movies and TV shows that produced them. “May the Force be with you.” “I’ll be back.” “You're gonna need a bigger boat.” You don't need to know the context. The words have long since transcended their original context.
body: Star Trek: The Original Series has plenty of those. Spock’s wish that everyone to “live long and prosper” is arguably the franchise's signature phrase. He also turned the simple word “fascinating” into a catchphrase simply by raising one eyebrow before saying it. Dr. McCoy (DeForest Kelley) spent three seasons reminding everyone, “I'm a doctor, not a…” and, at least in our collective memory declaring, “He's dead, Jim” while standing over the latest redshirt who wandered a little too far from the landing party.

On the surface, it doesn't seem like an obvious choice. It's not printed on T-shirts nearly as often as “live long and prosper.” It isn't endlessly quoted by people who have never watched an episode of Star Trek. And unlike “beam me up, Scotty,” it never became part of the broader pop culture vocabulary. But that's exactly why it's the best quote. It doesn't just capture Kirk. It captures the entire philosophy of Star Trek.
points: Certain lines of dialogue become so famous they almost stop belonging to the movies and TV shows that produced them.

highlights.title: Jean-Claude Van Damme's First Action Classic is Streaming for Free
highlights.summary: Jean-Claude Van Damme gets a bad rap. Due to when he got famous and the sorts of movies that he usually makes, JCVD often gets lumped in with other B-tier '80s action stars like Steven Seagal and Chuck Norris, which does Van Damme a disservice.
body: If you go back and watch the '80s action movies that made all three men famous, you'll likely notice the difference. Seagal and Norris both wade through most of their movies ( Executive Decision notwithstanding) like they're playing a video game with all the cheats enabled. Their characters rarely get wounded, have a moment's doubt about their current course of action, or even take a punch. To their credit, both Seagal and Norris made at least one genuinely good movie in their careers ( Under Siege, Lone Wolf McQuade, technically The Way of the Dragon ), but they both consistently played stoic invincible guys.

Van Damme, conversely, played more fallible protagonists, put up against more dangerous opposition. Van Damme's characters make mistakes ( Double Team, Double Impact ), get horribly beaten ( Cyborg, Kickboxer ), suffer serious losses along the way ( Timecop ), or just look like morons half the time ( Universal Soldier, his action mullet in Hard Target ). Even when Van Damme's acting isn't quite up to the task at hand (and y'know, you try putting on a performance in your second language), it's easier to root for him because it's easier to believe he's in danger.

highlights.title: The moment I knew: I admitted I had a crush on her. She replied, ‘Well, that’s good. Isn’t it?’
highlights.summary: Actors Peter Houghton and Anne Browning played lovers onstage, but a shared sense of humour and a magazine horoscope flipped the script on their real-life relationship. Find more stories from the moment I knew series. Anne and I met in Melbourne in 1997 when we were cast in a production of Hamlet.
body: At first it was a little awkward, but humour was the key. We’d sit on the dusty rehearsal room floor in our tracksuits while the director was working with another actor. Instead of practising our lines, we’d flip through the faded 70s magazines left in the corner and make jokes about what the models in flares or with chopped beards might be saying as they shot the images.

One day by chance I flipped to the horoscopes. I asked Anne what the stars could have in store for us in 1972. She told me her sign was Scorpio – the same as mine. My aim was just to laugh at the bullshit of horoscopes but when I read it out, it stopped me cold: “You have met someone now through work who will be one of the most important people in your life, perhaps a partner and soulmate.”

It was weird and uncanny but we just laughed it off. I felt embarrassed because it sounded like some kind of calculated romantic ploy. I quickly flicked to the next page but somewhere in my brain I knew it was the truth.
points: Actors Peter Houghton and Anne Browning played lovers onstage, but a shared sense of humour and a magazine horoscope flipped the script on their real-life relationship.

highlights.title: Blue Planet III is keeping the rough edges in the age of AI
highlights.summary: BBC's Blue Planet III is looking to prove its authenticity by leaving in the less-than-perfect shots. Previous incarnations of the nature series were defined by their gorgeous, crystal-clear footage that seemed almost too good to be real.
body: BBC’s Blue Planet III is keeping in shots that would normally end up on the cutting room floor to prove it’s real.

Executive Producer Elizabeth White told The Guardian in the past, “the amount of plankton and things” floating in the water would have caused them to cut a shot. Or “we might have framed out a boat or a buoy or gone: ‘Oh, actually … the water conditions are not really good enough for this.’” Instead, this time they’re leaving it all in to show a more authentic, organic version of the oceans.

The series features incredible displays of dolphins trapping fish by plugging holes with sea sponges, inter-species fish communication, and 200,000 crabs lining up in formation to feed. White says that real ocean creatures “are probably more remarkable than AI could imagine.”

highlights.title: 5 Most Perfect 1980s Games That Nobody Remembers
highlights.summary: The 1980s wasn't the decade video games were born; the origins of the medium go back a further 20 years, through the likes of Spacewar! and Pong. But it was in the 1980s that video games grew up, exploding in popularity and complexity and establishing many of their defining stars.
body: If you're ever lucky enough to see an original Tempest arcade cab, you have to try it; it's like nothing else. If not, the good news is that UK game programmer Jeff Minter was so obsessed with Tempest that he made multiple remakes of it, authorized and otherwise, which are easier to find and play today, including the peerlessly trippy Tempest 2000 (included in this collection for current hardware).

Mike Singleton's fantasy epic was a kind of Skyrim of the '80s. Heavily influenced by The Lord of the Rings, it was a hybrid of a role-playing game, a strategy game, and the "graphic adventures" of the time. It gave the player remarkable freedom to explore its fantasy kingdom, recruit new party members, and amass troops to combat the forces of an evil witch-king who has cursed the Land of Midnight with a permanent winter.

highlights.title: Supercell hit by cyberattack, but says no player data was affected
highlights.summary: The Clash of Clans developer says it was the target of multiple attacks last week and has notified police and regulators.
body: Supercell has confirmed that an unauthorised party has accessed a platform Supercell used to host company meetings and presentations.

In an announcement on October 21, the Clash of Clans developer said it was targeted by multiple cyberattacks last week, one of which caused the incident. Based on its investigations so far, Supercell believes no player data was affected.

It says it blocked further access, took the service offline and began investigating the platform and its security experts. It has since filed a police report, submitted a notification under the EU Cyber Resilience Act, and notified the Data Protection Ombudsman, but said that because the investigation is ongoing, it cannot share further details at this time.

The videos include current and former employees, as well as some guests and partners who took part in internal events. They may contain people’s names, images and voices, and the names and email addresses of the platform’s users were also accessed.

Antonelli will become world champion on Sunday if he wins the race while his Mercedes team-mate George Russell is lower than eighth and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton below fourth.

body: Twenty-five years into Kingdom Hearts, Square Enix has yet to establish a reliable formula for how the games represent various Disney worlds. Some levels simply insert Sora, Donald, and Goofy into a familiar story from movies like Mulan, Tarzan, or Aladdin. Agrabah returned in Kingdom Hearts 2 for a loose adaptation of The Return of Jafar, while Kingdom Hearts 3 used the setting of San Fransokyo to create a bona fide sequel to Big Hero 6.

We already know Kingdom Hearts 4 will send Sora into the Land of the Dead from Coco, while Mickey Mouse will explore a papercraft storybook world. A recent trailer revealed at D23 also confirms that Donald and Goofy visit Hades in the underworld looking for Sora, so it feels safe to assume that the world of Hercules, and presumably the Olympus Coliseum battle arena, is back. Those reveals still leave plenty of room for surprises. From one recent Disney blockbuster that feels practically designed for Kingdom Hearts to a long-rumored trip to a galaxy far, far away, here are the six worlds we hope to see — and five destinations we sincerely hope remain lost in Darkness forever.

highlights.title: Why your EV battery still loses charge while it's parked
highlights.summary: Electric vehicles lose battery when they're left unused for long periods. There are a number of reasons why, and some might be totally out of your control.
body: It's already costly enough to leave your EV at the airport for a week without it quietly discharging electricity while you're away. You could end up with a reduced battery percentage, even if the odometer hasn't budged. The truth is that an EV will lose a bit of charge while it's parked, but the amount lost will vary depending on the EV and what it has been doing while you were away.

There are a lot of factors involved when it comes to EV energy loss. Lithium-ion cells can lose charge naturally through electrolyte oxidation and reduction via a process called self-discharge. However, that is negligible compared with the electricity used while driving. The larger loss is from systems that continue to operate after you've locked the doors. It is not usually a problem over a weekend, but if you leave an EV unplugged for a couple of weeks, those little losses can begin to add up.

For reference, the DCU technically started with animated series Creature Commandos before heading to theaters with Superman. Peacemaker Season 2, Supergirl, Lanterns, and Clayface then followed.

While standalone Wonder Woman and Batman movies are in the cards, projects like The People v. Gorilla Grodd seem to be further along than most, with crossover moments mostly limited so far. So, what gives? Gunn has an easy answer that might leave impatient fans wanting more, but for him, it's a solution that will keep the DCU telling quality stories for years to come.

"I couldn't agree more," he said when replying to a fan defending the cinematic universe on Threads. "DCU is just an alternate universe; we can enter at any location or time and tell THAT story. I dislike the idea that individual stories aren't meaningful unless they lead to something else."

highlights.title: What kind of cooling system do EV batteries use and how does it work?
highlights.summary: Electric cars need incredibly large batteries that offer long driving ranges and charge quickly, but remain cool when under load. This is how they do so.
body: Have you ever pulled into a fast charging station on a freezing morning without notifying your EV first, and found that it charges more slowly? Turns out that if you set that same charger as a destination in the car's navigation, many EVs will use the time it takes to drive there to prepare the battery. It's something Tesla's manual tells owners to do 30 to 45 minutes before arriving, while Porsche goes so far as to warn that, without doing so, a vehicle's charging power might be lower.

This warm-up routine is part of an EV battery's thermal management system in most modern cars. Alongside it is usually a cooling loop, which uses liquid coolant pumped via tubes or metal plates pressed against the battery, collecting heat and carrying it to a radiator or into the car's air conditioning system.

Fleet management company Geotab tracked more than 22,700 EVs for a study and found that, on average, batteries lost 2.3 percent of their health each year. Cars in hot climates lost about 0.4 percentage points more a year than those in mild ones, while cars that frequently used fast chargers above 100 kW lost 3 percent a year against 1.5 percent for those that rarely did.

highlights.title: OpenAI now trains its frontier AI models with no internet access
highlights.summary: OpenAI is now training its most advanced AI models without internet access following a string of rogue hacking incidents. In a blog post on Friday, OpenAI says it built an offline testing environment where AI models can interact with indexed and cached web content "without risk of affecting…
body: OpenAI paused training its frontier AI models in September, after disclosing several incidents in which its AI agents broke out of their testing environments to hack third-party companies and government agencies, or swarm obscure websites. On October 1st, OpenAI resumed reinforcement learning training and internal inference with tighter security measures, the blog post says.

Reading data from the cache is faster than retrieving it from main memory, and the agents used this timing difference to communicate. One agent encoded information by evicting selected data from the cache. Another timed how long it took to reload that data, using the difference between fast and slow reads to recover the message. Once the agents agreed on a protocol for encoding and decoding these signals, they could exchange the synthetic secrets without changing a shared file or opening a network connection.

OpenAI says it has added checks to its monitoring system to detect this type of communication. It will also continue training its frontier AI models without a network connection until improved safeguards “justify broader internet access.”

body: "And, yes, there's violence, and there's hardware, and equipment, and there's killing – but underneath it I think the game, and the craters of the game, are really looking at the cost of war, the cost of having to be a warrior who's, for whatever reason, chosen to put himself between real danger and the rest of us, and the burden that these guys carry."

Berg seems to be putting in the work to nail a Modern Warfare story for the big screen, but not every fan is convinced that he's the right guy for the job. That's mostly because he had some not-so-nice things to say about gaming back in 2013. When asked for his take on video games based on war at the time, he said, called them "pathetic," using the term, "keyboard courage."
"I think anyone that sits around playing video games for four hours... It's weak," Berg elaborated at the time. "Get out, do something."

These days he's changed his tune, and judging by his affection for characters like Captain Price and Ghost, he's hoping to do right by Modern Warfare and its fans. His upcoming film, The Mosquito Bowl, is a sports-war film set to premiere later this month. His vision for the Call of Duty movie will start to take shape after that.
